claim: V2HeR3 from Emiliania huxleyi virus 202 is a light-activated proton transporter.
source: Here, we report that a viral HeR from Emiliania huxleyi virus 202 (V2HeR3) is a light-activated proton transporter.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by electrophysiological data presented in the manuscript.

claim: V2HeR3 absorbs blue-green light.
source: V2HeR3 absorbs blue-green light, and the active intermediate contains the deprotonated retinal Schiff base.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 2A shows the absorption spectrum with a maximum at 500 nm.

claim: The active intermediate of V2HeR3 contains the deprotonated retinal Schiff base.
source: V2HeR3 absorbs blue-green light, and the active intermediate contains the deprotonated retinal Schiff base.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 2 shows the M intermediate formation which is characteristic of Schiff base deprotonation.

claim: E191 in TM6 constitutes the gate together with the retinal Schiff base in V2HeR3.
source: Site-directed mutagenesis study revealed that E191 in TM6 constitutes the gate together with the retinal Schiff base.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 3 shows that E191Q mutation abolishes photocurrent while E191D retains activity.

claim: E205 and E215 form a PAG (proton accepting group) of the Schiff base in V2HeR3.
source: E205 and E215 form a PAG of the Schiff base, and mutations at these positions converted the protein into an outward proton pump.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 3B shows that E205Q and E215Q mutations result in positive photocurrents at all voltages tested.

claim: Mutations at E205 and E215 converted V2HeR3 into an outward proton pump.
source: E205 and E215 form a PAG of the Schiff base, and mutations at these positions converted the protein into an outward proton pump.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 3B shows that E205Q and E215Q mutations result in positive photocurrents indicating outward proton transport.

claim: Three environmental viral HeRs from the same group as V2HeR3 exhibited similar proton-transport activity.
source: Three environmental viral HeRs from the same group as well as a more distantly related HeR exhibited similar proton-transport activity, indicating that HeR functions might be diverse similarly to type-1 microbial rhodopsins.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 4B shows photocurrents from VPS401HeR, VTara5482HeR, VTara4616HeR, and VTara8957HeR.

claim: HeR functions might be diverse similarly to type-1 microbial rhodopsins.
source: Three environmental viral HeRs from the same group as well as a more distantly related HeR exhibited similar proton-transport activity, indicating that HeR functions might be diverse similarly to type-1 microbial rhodopsins.
evidence: The abstract states this as an inference from the observation of different HeR activities.

claim: Some strains of E. huxleyi contain one HeR that is related to the viral HeRs.
source: Some strains of E. huxleyi contain one HeR that is related to the viral HeRs, while its viruses EhV-201 and EhV-202 contain two and three HeRs, respectively.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 1A shows EhHeR in the phylogenetic tree.

claim: EhV-201 contains two HeRs.
source: Some strains of E. huxleyi contain one HeR that is related to the viral HeRs, while its viruses EhV-201 and EhV-202 contain two and three HeRs, respectively.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 4A shows V1HeR1 and V1HeR2.

claim: EhV-202 contains three HeRs.
source: Some strains of E. huxleyi contain one HeR that is related to the viral HeRs, while its viruses EhV-201 and EhV-202 contain two and three HeRs, respectively.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 4A shows V2HeR1, V2HeR2, and V2HeR3.

claim: Except for V2HeR3 from EhV-202, none of the other HeRs from E. huxleyi and its viruses exhibit ion transport activity.
source: Except for V2HeR3 from EhV-202, none of these proteins exhibit ion transport activity.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 4A shows that only V2HeR3 exhibits steady-state photocurrent.

claim: When expressed in E. huxleyi cell membranes, V2HeR3 has the potential to depolarize the host cells by light.
source: Thus, when expressed in the E. huxleyi cell membranes, only V2HeR3 has the potential to depolarize the host cells by light, possibly to overcome the host defense mechanisms or to prevent superinfection.
evidence: The abstract states this as a speculation based on the observed inward proton transport activity.

claim: V2HeR3 depolarization of host cells may help overcome host defense mechanisms or prevent superinfection.
source: Thus, when expressed in the E. huxleyi cell membranes, only V2HeR3 has the potential to depolarize the host cells by light, possibly to overcome the host defense mechanisms or to prevent superinfection.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a speculative explanation for the function of V2HeR3.

claim: V2HeR3 can potentially be used as an optogenetic tool.
source: The neuronal activity generated by V2HeR3 suggests that it can potentially be used as an optogenetic tool, similarly to type-1 microbial rhodopsins.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 1E-G show that V2HeR3 can trigger action potentials in neurons.

claim: Rhodopsins convert light into signals and energy in animals and microbes.
source: Rhodopsins convert light into signals and energy in animals and microbes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Heliorhodopsins (HeRs) are a recently discovered new rhodopsin family.
source: Heliorhodopsins (HeRs), a recently discovered new rhodopsin family, are widely present in archaea, bacteria, unicellular eukaryotes, and giant viruses, but their function remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citation to Pushkarev et al., 2018.

claim: HeRs are widely present in archaea, bacteria, unicellular eukaryotes, and giant viruses.
source: Heliorhodopsins (HeRs), a recently discovered new rhodopsin family, are widely present in archaea, bacteria, unicellular eukaryotes, and giant viruses, but their function remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citation to Pushkarev et al., 2018.

claim: The function of HeRs remains unknown (prior to this study).
source: Heliorhodopsins (HeRs), a recently discovered new rhodopsin family, are widely present in archaea, bacteria, unicellular eukaryotes, and giant viruses, but their function remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as the context for the current study.

claim: Rhodopsins are classified into type-1 microbial and type-2 animal rhodopsins.
source: Rhodopsins are classified into type-1 microbial and type-2 animal rhodopsins, which contain all-trans and 11-cis retinal, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Type-1 microbial rhodopsins contain all-trans retinal.
source: Rhodopsins are classified into type-1 microbial and type-2 animal rhodopsins, which contain all-trans and 11-cis retinal, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Type-2 animal rhodopsins contain 11-cis retinal.
source: Rhodopsins are classified into type-1 microbial and type-2 animal rhodopsins, which contain all-trans and 11-cis retinal, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Type-2 animal rhodopsins function as G-protein-coupled receptors.
source: Type-2 animal rhodopsins function as G-protein-coupled receptors, while the molecular functions of type-1 microbial rhodopsins are highly diverse and include light-driven ion pumps, light-gated ion channels, light sensors, and light-activated enzymes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: The molecular functions of type-1 microbial rhodopsins are highly diverse and include light-driven ion pumps, light-gated ion channels, light sensors, and light-activated enzymes.
source: Type-2 animal rhodopsins function as G-protein-coupled receptors, while the molecular functions of type-1 microbial rhodopsins are highly diverse and include light-driven ion pumps, light-gated ion channels, light sensors, and light-activated enzymes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Ion-transporting rhodopsins are used as the main tools to control membrane potential in optogenetics.
source: Ion-transporting rhodopsins are used as the main tools to control membrane potential in optogenetics (Deisseroth and Hegemann, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citation.

claim: HeRs were recently discovered using functional metagenomics.
source: In addition to type-1 and type-2 rhodopsins, a previously unrecognized divergent family of heliorhodopsins (HeRs) was recently discovered using functional metagenomics (Pushkarev et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citation.

claim: HeRs are distant relatives of type-1 rhodopsins.
source: HeRs are distant relatives of type-1 rhodopsins, and their structures and photocycles resemble those of other microbial rhodopsins (Kovalev et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Pushkarev et al., 2018; Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: The structures and photocycles of HeRs resemble those of other microbial rhodopsins.
source: HeRs are distant relatives of type-1 rhodopsins, and their structures and photocycles resemble those of other microbial rhodopsins (Kovalev et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020; Pushkarev et al., 2018; Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: The most unusual structural feature of HeRs is that their membrane topology is inverted compared to type-1 and -2 rhodopsins.
source: The most unusual structural feature of HeRs is that their membrane topology is inverted compared to type-1 and -2 rhodopsins (Pushkarev et al., 2018; Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Previous studies did not detect any ion transport activity in HeRs.
source: Previous studies did not detect any ion transport activity in HeRs, and based on their slow photocycle, a sensory function was suggested (Pushkarev et al., 2018; Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Based on their slow photocycle, a sensory function was suggested for HeRs.
source: Previous studies did not detect any ion transport activity in HeRs, and based on their slow photocycle, a sensory function was suggested (Pushkarev et al., 2018; Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: The crystal structures of TaHeR and 48C12 show that the interior of the extracellular half is highly hydrophobic.
source: Analogously, no ion-transport function is consistent with the crystal structures of the prokaryotic HeRs TaHeR (from a Thermoplasmatales archaeon) (Shihoya et al., 2019) and 48C12 (from an actinobacterium) (Kovalev et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2020), in which the interior of the extracellular half is highly hydrophobic.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: HeRs are a highly diverse group.
source: It should be noted, however, that these structures provide a very limited representation of the family. HeRs are a highly diverse group (Kovalev et al., 2020; Chazan et al., 2022) for which a variety of functions might be expected.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: The HeRs studied here come from giant double-stranded DNA viruses from the genus Coccolithovirus (Phycodnaviridae) that infect the microalga E. huxleyi.
source: The HeRs studied here come from giant double-stranded DNA viruses from the genus Coccolithovirus (Phycodnaviridae) that infect the microalga E. huxleyi (=Gephyrocapsa huxleyi).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: E. huxleyi is a globally important marine coccolithophore whose massive blooms are observable from satellites and have an impact on Earth's climate.
source: E. huxleyi is a globally important marine coccolithophore whose massive blooms are observable from satellites and have an impact on Earth's climate (Thierstein and Young, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citation.

claim: E. huxleyi viruses are able to collapse its blooms and thus represent one of the main factors controlling abundance of E. huxleyi in the ocean.
source: E. huxleyi viruses are able to collapse its blooms and thus represent one of the main factors controlling abundance of E. huxleyi in the ocean (Bidle et al., 2007; Vardi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Coccolithoviruses encode HeRs in their genomes, with some isolates, such as EhV-202, having up to three HeR genes.
source: Curiously, coccolithoviruses encode HeRs in their genomes, with some isolates, such as EhV-202, having up to three HeR genes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: One of the HeR genes from EhV-202 (AET42570.1; V2HeR2) has been expressed before and failed to demonstrate any light-dependent ion-transporting activity.
source: One of the HeR genes from EhV-202 (AET42570.1; V2HeR2) has been expressed before and failed to demonstrate any light-dependent ion-transporting activity (Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citation.

claim: V2HeR3 has only ~30% identity to V2HeR2.
source: Driven by the hypothesis that there might exist a functional diversity among the three HeRs in EhV-202, we first targeted V2HeR3 (AET42421.1), a HeR with only ~30% identity to V2HeR2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The C-terminus of V2HeR3 faces the extracellular side.
source: Clear membrane fluorescence from anti-cMyc tag was observed only from the C-terminal cMyc, but not from the N-terminal cMyc (magenta in Figure 1B), indicating that the C-terminus faces the extracellular side, as in other HeRs (Pushkarev et al., 2018; Shihoya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: V2HeR3-expressing ND7/23 cells yielded consistent photocurrent responses in patch-clamp experiments.
source: Remarkably, the V3HeR-expressing ND7/23 cells yielded consistent photocurrent responses in the patch-clamp experiments (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The photocurrents of V2HeR3 exhibited a sharp negative transient peak (I0), which rapidly dropped into a relatively broad peak component (I1), followed by a steady-state current component (I2) during the course of illumination.
source: The photocurrents exhibited a sharp negative transient peak (I0), which rapidly dropped into a relatively broad peak component (I1), followed by a steady-state current component (I2) during the course of illumination.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The presence of steady-state currents is an unequivocal indication of ion transport maintained for a long time span.
source: The presence of steady-state currents is an unequivocal indication of ion transport maintained for a long time span (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Photocurrent amplitude of V2HeR3 increased with light intensity and demonstrated a single sigmoid curve.
source: Photocurrent amplitude increased with light intensity and demonstrated a single sigmoid curve (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicative of photocurrents owing to single-photon events by unphotolyzed molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The single sigmoid curve of photocurrent amplitude vs. light intensity is indicative of photocurrents owing to single-photon events by unphotolyzed molecules.
source: Photocurrent amplitude increased with light intensity and demonstrated a single sigmoid curve (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicative of photocurrents owing to single-photon events by unphotolyzed molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Components I1 and I2 of V2HeR3 photocurrent exhibited a linear relation to the voltage in the I-V plot.
source: Components I1 and I2 exhibited a linear relation to the voltage in the current-voltage (I-V) plot (see Figure 1C), with a reversal potential (Erev) at +30 and +40 mV, respectively, while I0 was always negatively directed and exhibits a weak voltage dependency.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The reversal potential (Erev) of I1 is at +30 mV.
source: Components I1 and I2 exhibited a linear relation to the voltage in the current-voltage (I-V) plot (see Figure 1C), with a reversal potential (Erev) at +30 and +40 mV, respectively, while I0 was always negatively directed and exhibits a weak voltage dependency.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The reversal potential (Erev) of I2 is at +40 mV.
source: Components I1 and I2 exhibited a linear relation to the voltage in the current-voltage (I-V) plot (see Figure 1C), with a reversal potential (Erev) at +30 and +40 mV, respectively, while I0 was always negatively directed and exhibits a weak voltage dependency.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: I0 of V2HeR3 photocurrent was always negatively directed and exhibits a weak voltage dependency.
source: Components I1 and I2 exhibited a linear relation to the voltage in the current-voltage (I-V) plot (see Figure 1C), with a reversal potential (Erev) at +30 and +40 mV, respectively, while I0 was always negatively directed and exhibits a weak voltage dependency.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The passive currents of I1 and I2 imply a light-gated channel function.
source: The passive currents of I1 and I2 imply a light-gated channel function (Figure 1C) and the linear I-V relationship suggests that V2HeR3 is a voltage-independent channel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The linear I-V relationship suggests that V2HeR3 is a voltage-independent channel.
source: The passive currents of I1 and I2 imply a light-gated channel function (Figure 1C) and the linear I-V relationship suggests that V2HeR3 is a voltage-independent channel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0 resulted in an Erev shift from +40 to +70 mV for V2HeR3.
source: Lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0 resulted in an Erev shift from +40 to +70 mV (Figure 1D), while a shift from +40 to -6 mV was observed when pHi was lowered (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Lowering the intracellular pH resulted in an Erev shift from +40 to -6 mV for V2HeR3.
source: Lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0 resulted in an Erev shift from +40 to +70 mV (Figure 1D), while a shift from +40 to -6 mV was observed when pHi was lowered (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Replacing the solutions with Na+ or K+ did not show any significant Erev shift for V2HeR3.
source: By contrast, replacing the solutions with Na+ or K+ did not show any significant Erev shift (Figure 1D), suggesting that V2HeR3 is a light-gated proton channel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1D.

claim: V2HeR3 is a light-gated proton channel.
source: By contrast, replacing the solutions with Na+ or K+ did not show any significant Erev shift (Figure 1D), suggesting that V2HeR3 is a light-gated proton channel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the pH and cation replacement experiments.

claim: There was a statistically significant difference in the current amplitude of V2HeR3 in the presence of K+.
source: There was nevertheless a statistically significant difference in the current amplitude in the presence of K+ (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The H+ transport of V2HeR3 is somehow enhanced in the presence of K+ at the extracellular side.
source: This indicates that the H+ transport is somehow enhanced in the presence of K+ at the extracellular side.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: ChR2 possesses an outward proton pump activity and is thus a leaky proton pump.
source: It should be noted in this respect that channelrhodopsin 2 from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (ChR2) (Nagel et al., 2003), a standard depolarization tool in optogenetics (Boyden et al., 2005; Deisseroth and Hegemann, 2017; Ishizuka et al., 2006), possesses an outward proton pump activity and is thus a leaky proton pump (Feldbauer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by citations.

claim: At low extracellular pH, the outward proton flux of GR changes to a passive influx.
source: Similarly, at low extracellular pH, the outward proton flux of the proton pump rhodopsin from Gloeobacter violaceus (GR) changes to a passive influx (Vogt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by citation.

claim: Significant positive Erev suggests that V2HeR3 also possesses the activity of a proton pump, although the direction is inward.
source: In the case of V2HeR3, significant positive Erev suggests that V2HeR3 also possesses the activity of a proton pump, although the direction is inward.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The Erev shift upon pH change is smaller than that expected from Nernst potential for V2HeR3.
source: The Erev shift upon pH change is smaller than that expected from Nernst potential (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0 (ΔpH = 1.4) is expected to correspond to a shift of 82 mV according to Nernst potential.
source: Lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0 (ΔpH = 1.4) is expected to correspond to a shift of 82 mV, yet only a 40–60 mV shift was observed for V2HeR3 (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a calculation based on the Nernst equation.

claim: Only a 40–60 mV shift was observed for V2HeR3 when lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0.
source: Lowering the extracellular pH from 7.4 to 6.0 (ΔpH = 1.4) is expected to correspond to a shift of 82 mV, yet only a 40–60 mV shift was observed for V2HeR3 (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The ionic current of V2HeR3 includes an H+-pump component which is responsible for the deviation from the Nernst equation.
source: We thus conclude that the ionic current of V2HeR3 includes an H+-pump component which is responsible for the deviation from the Nernst equation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the Erev shift data.

claim: The current amplitude and the Erev of V2HeR3 were altered depending on the monovalent anions in the solution.
source: The current amplitude and the Erev were also altered depending on the monovalent anions in the solution (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The inward current (I1 and I2) of V2HeR3 was suppressed in the presence of Cl−, Br−, and NO3− in the bath solution.
source: The inward current (I1 and I2) was suppressed in the presence of Cl−, Br−, and NO3− in the bath solution (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B right) and the Erev values shifted accordingly (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B left).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: No significant change either in the current amplitude or in the Erev of V2HeR3 was observed when Asp− in the pipette solution was replaced with Cl− or SO42−.
source: On the other hand, no significant change either in the current amplitude or in the Erev was observed when Asp− in the pipette solution was replaced with Cl− or SO42− (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C right).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C.

claim: V2HeR3 contains a binding site for a monovalent anion at the extracellular side.
source: Our interpretation of these results is that V2HeR3 contains a binding site for a monovalent anion at the extracellular side, and anion binding affects proton transport.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the anion replacement experiments.

claim: Anion binding affects proton transport in V2HeR3.
source: Our interpretation of these results is that V2HeR3 contains a binding site for a monovalent anion at the extracellular side, and anion binding affects proton transport.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the anion replacement experiments.

claim: V2HeR3 functions as a proton channel with active inward H+ transport.
source: Summarizing these electrophysiological experiments, we conclude that V2HeR3 functions as a proton channel with active inward H+ transport.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the electrophysiological experiments.

claim: Illumination of V2HeR3-expressing yeast cells increased solution pH.
source: Illumination of the V2HeR3-expressing yeast cells increased solution pH, which was abolished by the addition of the proton uncoupler CCCP (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The light-induced pH increase in V2HeR3-expressing yeast cells was abolished by the addition of the proton uncoupler CCCP.
source: Illumination of the V2HeR3-expressing yeast cells increased solution pH, which was abolished by the addition of the proton uncoupler CCCP (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The fast inward-directed current I0 of V2HeR3 was significantly larger than I1 and I2.
source: The fast inward-directed current I0 was significantly larger than I1 and I2 and the current-voltage relationship of I0 was dramatically shifted to positive values with respect to the reversal potential (Figure 1C1–V plot, left).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The current-voltage relationship of I0 was dramatically shifted to positive values with respect to the reversal potential.
source: The fast inward-directed current I0 was significantly larger than I1 and I2 and the current-voltage relationship of I0 was dramatically shifted to positive values with respect to the reversal potential (Figure 1C1–V plot, left).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Extrapolation of the voltage dependence of I0 predicted its reversal potential as +290 mV.
source: Extrapolation of the voltage dependence of I0 predicted its reversal potential as +290 mV, indicating that I0 is due to an ion pump component.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an analysis of the I-V data.

claim: I0 is due to an ion pump component.
source: Extrapolation of the voltage dependence of I0 predicted its reversal potential as +290 mV, indicating that I0 is due to an ion pump component.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the extrapolated reversal potential.

claim: No significant change in I0 was observed when NMG+ in the extracellular solution was replaced with Na+.
source: No significant change was observed when NMG+ in the extracellular solution was replaced with Na+, or when pHe was lowered from 7.4 to 6.0 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: No significant change in I0 was observed when pHe was lowered from 7.4 to 6.0.
source: No significant change was observed when NMG+ in the extracellular solution was replaced with Na+, or when pHe was lowered from 7.4 to 6.0 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: A substantial reduction in the I0 current amplitude was observed when pHi was lowered to 6.0.
source: However, a substantial reduction in the current amplitude was observed when pHi was lowered to 6.0, but it was not affected by replacement of Na+ as the intracellular cation (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: I0 was not affected by replacement of Na+ as the intracellular cation.
source: However, a substantial reduction in the current amplitude was observed when pHi was lowered to 6.0, but it was not affected by replacement of Na+ as the intracellular cation (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6A.

claim: No significant differences in the I-V plot of I0 were observed when comparing Asp−, Cl−, and SO42−.
source: Further, no significant differences in the I-V plot were observed when comparing Asp−, Cl−, and SO42− (Figure 1—figure supplement 6C and D), suggesting that anions do not contribute to I0.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6C and D.

claim: Anions do not contribute to I0.
source: Further, no significant differences in the I-V plot were observed when comparing Asp−, Cl−, and SO42− (Figure 1—figure supplement 6C and D), suggesting that anions do not contribute to I0.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the anion replacement experiments.

claim: The component I₀ reached its negative peak at 0.85 ms, independently from the membrane voltage.
source: The component I₀ reached its negative peak at 0.85 ms, independently from the membrane voltage (Figure 1—figure supplement 7A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7A and B.

claim: The peak of I0 exhibited exponential relaxation with two time constants (τoff).
source: The peak exhibited exponential relaxation with two time constants (τoff) (Figure 1—figure supplement 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7C.

claim: The inward-directed H+ transport and H+ exclusion are suppressed by high proton concentrations (pH 6.0) at the cytoplasmic side.
source: Taken together, these observations could be interpreted as evidence that the inward-directed H+ transport and H+ exclusion are suppressed by high proton concentrations (pH 6.0) at the cytoplasmic side.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the pH dependence of I0.

claim: It is difficult to distinguish ionic current from an intramolecular charge displacement for the I0 component.
source: In spite of the detailed experiments on the I0 component above, it is difficult to distinguish ionic current from an intramolecular charge displacement.
